messages.author: 453ddfeccaf29bbb
messages.subject: sampling from final variational approximation
parts:
hi all,

sorry for the many messages, but i think i'm going to need this for the journal version of the paper that we're writing up right now.

what is "this"? for ADVI it's a function that takes in a multivariate Gaussian over the parameters, draws a bunch of points from said Gaussian, and pushes the samples through transformations defined by a model.

so i think this puts me in the position of implementing this. i was wondering if i should start from scratch or if anyone has written anything towards this goal.

apologies in advance if i missed any discussion around this in the past few weeks/months.

cheers
alp

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] sampling from final variational approximation
parts:
We need that for MLE and MML, too. The one you want to
coordinate with is Rob Trangucci, who's in charge of the MLE
and MML efforts.

The code should probably go somewhere more general than in
with VB, like in the model utility class.

I'm happy to chime in on design, but it should be relatively
simple. We have the multi_normal_rng function already defined.
And the transform is available through the generated model code,
though it's not pretty to use standalone.

What we really need to do is change the model, which currently
uses the method write_array to convert the array of unconstrained
parameters to an array of constrained parameters. Then there
are methods to pull out the parameter names and sizes/dimesnions
in the order they're generated by the model. Just be careful to
keep in mind it's last-index major (column major for matrices).

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] sampling from final variational approximation
parts:
More specifically,

// Get constrained parameter names
std::vector<std::string> names;
model.constrained_param_names(names, true, true);

// construct mean, mu, and covariance, C.
L = cholesky(C);
for (int n = 0; n < size; ++n) z(n) = normal_rng(0, 1);
q = L* z + mu;

model.write_array(rng,
q, // Input unconstrained values
model_values, // Output constrained values
true, true,
msg_stream_);

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] sampling from final variational approximation
parts:
Good point --- using the Cholesky parameterization is much better than
using multi_normal_rng(). There are examples of just this in the GP
section of the manual.

Is it possible to do even better somehow by rescaling uniform(0,1) variates
directly? I know you can do inverse CDFs, but that's unlikely to be a
computational win over normal_rng() or Boost would've implemented normal
RNGs that way.

- Bob
